reviewed_inputs: src/components/Header, Hero, ServicesSection, DeliveryCenters, Footer, MasterDataView, MasterDataTable

decisions.topic: Fate of marketing components (Header, Hero, ServicesSection, DeliveryCenters, Footer)
decisions.decision: Retire from the default app tree. §0 defines this product as an internal management application, not a public marketing site — a marketing landing page is out of the product's actual scope, and CLAUDE.md §1 (No Unused Code) forbids keeping dead components around 'just in case'. Downstream (Solution Architect / Developer) should remove Hero, ServicesSection, DeliveryCenters and the marketing Header/Footer from the render tree entirely rather than hiding them behind a route no one requested. Git history preserves the code if a public page is wanted later — that is a new feature request, not a revert.
decisions.rationale: Avoids duplicate/parallel 'two apps in one App.jsx' architecture and dead code that will bit-rot.
decisions.risk_if_ignored: A conditional (hash-based or route-based) fork between 'marketing mode' and 'app mode' baked into App.jsx becomes permanent accidental complexity and an untested code path.

decisions.decision: Do NOT adopt a router library (react-router or similar) at this stage. package.json currently has zero non-React dependencies; frontend.md's 'no global state library unless the team decides otherwise' spirit extends to routing — minimal footprint until multiple real routes justify it. Extend the existing useLocationHash pattern into a small, named route registry (e.g. `src/lib/routes.js` exporting `{ path, label, component }` entries) that AppShell's nav renders from. This is a directive, not a suggestion left open for the Solution Architect to re-litigate — a new dependency for one real route (Master Data) plus placeholder nav items is disproportionate.
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md §1 Simplicity First / Minimal Impact. No dependency-adoption need has been demonstrated.

decisions.topic: Nav/route registry location — explorer's suggestion to extend masterDataApi.js's MASTER_DATA_TABLES pattern
decisions.decision: REJECTED as proposed. Do not add nav/route entries into `src/lib/masterDataApi.js`. That module's job is the Master Data fetch layer; folding unrelated app-shell navigation config into it is inappropriate coupling (a change to nav has no reason to touch the data-fetching module, and vice versa). Use a separate `src/lib/routes.js` (or `src/config/nav.js`) for the nav/route registry. The 'columns drive rendering' array-config *idiom* is fine to reuse — just not the same file/module.
decisions.rationale: Single-responsibility per module; this is exactly the 'inappropriate coupling' this review stage exists to catch (agent role definition).
decisions.risk_if_ignored: masterDataApi.js becomes a dumping ground for unrelated config; future data-layer changes risk breaking navigation and vice versa.

decisions.decision: APPROVED as BA specified. MasterDataView/MasterDataTable + useMasterDataTable's {data, isLoading, error} contract is the one existing internal-app pattern and MUST be reused/generalized (e.g. into a shared DataTable primitive), not reimplemented in parallel. Any new dashboard view built with its own bespoke fetch/loading logic instead of the existing hook contract is a duplicate-solution violation and should be rejected at the Architecture Critic (3.1) or Code Reviewer (4.2) stage if it appears.
decisions.rationale: Reject duplicate-of-existing-solution per this stage's mandate; frontend.md's hook contract is already the standard.
decisions.risk_if_ignored: Two competing data-fetching patterns in one small codebase.

decisions.topic: Signed-in-user context with no auth backend
decisions.decision: Placeholder/display-only, explicitly and visibly non-functional (e.g. a static mock user object in a constants file, clearly named `MOCK_CURRENT_USER` or similar) — not wired to any fake login flow, fake token, or fake session storage. No behavior beyond rendering a name/avatar/menu affordance is in scope. This must be easy to find and swap out wholesale when real auth is built (single source of truth for the mock, not scattered inline).
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md §23 confirms no backend/auth exists; §1 Security by Default — never fabricate the appearance of a working auth boundary.
decisions.risk_if_ignored: A convincing-looking but fake 'signed in' UI could be mistaken for real auth later and shipped without an actual security review.

decisions.decision: New/changed components produced by this feature MUST add PropTypes at the top of the file, per frontend.md's existing (previously unenforced) rule. This is not optional cleanup scope-creep — it's applying a standing convention to new code, which is exactly what frontend.md already requires; the fact that older components never did it is pre-existing debt, not license to keep skipping it. Do not do a repo-wide PropTypes retrofit as part of this feature — that is out of scope (would violate Minimal Impact).
decisions.rationale: frontend.md §Components; CLAUDE.md §1 Minimal Impact bounds the retrofit.

decisions.decision: APPROVED as BA specified (REQ-5). Extend `:root` in src/index.css with new tokens (e.g. `--color-surface`, `--color-sidebar-bg`, elevation tokens) rather than a parallel token set. No hardcoded hex values in new CSS Modules. CSS Modules co-location pattern (Component.jsx/.module.css/index.js) continues unchanged.
decisions.rationale: frontend.md Styling section; no violation risk identified.

decisions.topic: State management for shell (active nav item, current user, sidebar collapse, etc.)
decisions.decision: Local component state / a single small AppShell-scoped Context if truly cross-cutting (e.g. current-user, active-route) — no global state library. This is a direct application of frontend.md's existing rule, restated here because app-shell work is exactly the kind of feature where a Redux/Zustand-style dependency gets proposed 'for convenience'. Reject any such proposal at Tech Lead (2.5) or Architecture Critic (3.1) if it surfaces.

flags_for_tech_lead_and_solution_archite: Confirm the new route registry module name/location (proposal: src/lib/routes.js) before SDD is written, so System Engineer (3.3) doesn't invent a second competing location.

Confirm removal (not hiding) of marketing components is acceptable to the owner before Developer stage deletes them — this is a product-scope call, not just a code call, and this review is not the owner's sign-off.

Watch for scope creep into installing a UI kit or icon library 'to make the sidebar look right' — no such dependency has been justified; if one is genuinely needed, it must be an explicit, named architecture decision at stage 2.5/3.1, not an incidental add.
summary: Reviewed the Business Analyst's FEAT-1 brief against the existing codebase architecture and frontend.md/CLAUDE.md conventions. No idea in the brief is rejected outright, but several implementation directions implied or left open are resolved here to prevent architecture drift before any code is written: no router library adoption (extend hash-routing via a new, separate route-registry module — explicitly NOT folded into masterDataApi.js, which would be inappropriate coupling), retire the marketing components rather than fork the app between 'marketing mode' and 'app mode', keep the signed-in-user context strictly placeholder/mock (no fake auth flow), reuse (never duplicate) the existing MasterDataTable/useMasterDataTable pattern for all new data-dense views, apply frontend.md's already-standing PropTypes rule to new components only, and continue the no-global-state-library / token-reuse conventions already in force. No blocking findings — verdict PASS. Read-only architecture review; no application code was created or edited in this stage.
